description: One ask a task raised, opened in a tab of its own (titled with the task's name, an alarm icon): who it's from and ⋯, its Markdown body with pictures, its form, its buttons and Route to…, and a message box at the foot that writes to the asking task's Bot. Full width.
opens: a card's title in the Inbox
back / forward in the tab history

phone.does: A screen of its own opened from the Inbox, titled with the task's name, Back returns to the Inbox
phone.why: One column at a time on a phone

parts.name: From line
parts.shows: The asking Bot's picture, then "from Task “<task>” on <host>" (dim, small), as a message's from line; at the end, on a stopped ask "Not answered — the task stopped", on one sent to a Bot "Sent to <Bot>", and ⋯.

parts.name: ⋯ menu
parts.shows: History: every version of the ask with when it came ("v2 · today 10:42"), the one shown ticked; picking one shows it (its buttons work only on the latest). On a stopped ask, Remove too.

parts.name: Body
parts.shows: The task's Markdown, as a message is drawn: headings, bold, lists, code, tables. A picture on a line of its own is as wide as the text, its height as its shape has it, rounded; a table cell holding only a picture shows it; never a file path. Click a picture to see it large (the image viewer).

parts.name: Form
parts.shows: The ask's fields as setting rows (TaskField's types): text, a field that fills the row's width with its label in it; number, an entry at the row's end; on/off, a switch; choice, a drop-down. The person fills them; Meta may fill them for them to check.

parts.name: Buttons
parts.shows: The task's buttons, each sized to its label, wrapping as whole buttons when a row is full (Adw.WrapBox; the phone's FlowRow): style primary (the accent), secondary (plain), or a colour of the accent palette (blue, teal, green, yellow, orange, red, pink, purple, slate: schema/tokens accent.*); a picture button shows its picture over its label. Route to… at the row's end.

actions.does: Answers the ask: its task is told which button, with the form's values, and the ask leaves every Inbox. There's no separate Submit.

parts.name: Route to…
parts.shows: A flat menu button: "Have a model answer", then the ask's host's models as the model picker lists them; "Send to a Bot", then that host's Bots with their pictures.

actions.does: The model is asked to answer; meanwhile "<model> is answering…" over the buttons. Its answer fills the form and says "<model> would press “<button>”" with its reason; nothing takes effect till the person presses a button (the model's, or another, the form as they leave it). Dismiss lets it go.
The ask is sent to that Bot, which answers it with its answer_ask tool (the one way a Bot's answer takes effect without the person pressing); the ask stays, "Sent to <Bot>", till it does.

parts.name: Model's answer
parts.shows: Over the buttons while a model's answer waits: "<model> would press “<button>”" (bold) and its reason, with Dismiss; that button drawn as the suggested one. While it's asked: "<model> is answering…" with a spinner. Failed: "<model> couldn't answer: <why>".

parts.name: Message box
parts.shows: The composer at the foot, its send button's tooltip "Send to <Bot>" (the asking task's Bot).

actions.does: What's written goes to the asking task's Bot as a message, with the ask; the Bot may propose an answer (answer_ask: shown over the buttons as a model's is, for the person to confirm, never pressing for them) or put a new version of it (revise_ask), which shows here at once.

states.name: stopped
states.shows: Its task went away unanswered: the body's first heading struck through and the body greyed, "Not answered — the task stopped" on the from line, form and buttons off, Route to… off, the box still writes to the Bot.

states.name: answered elsewhere
states.shows: Answered on another device (or by a Bot): the tab says "This ask is no longer waiting" and its buttons are off.

decisions.said: Tasks render their asks the way a person formats a message: markdown, tables that can hold images.
decisions.rule: Every app draws an ask's body as a message's Markdown, a table cell holding only a picture showing it.

decisions.said: A living, versioned artefact with buttons that evolve it, messages to agents, closing with the deterministic task.
decisions.rule: Every app shows an ask's versions, its buttons and a message box to the asking task's Bot. A press answers the version it was pressed on, and the host refuses it once the ask has a newer one; the task may put a new version of an ask that was pressed, which opens the same ask again, waiting, with its History.

decisions.said: "Versions" is the wrong word: the picker becomes ⋯ → History.
decisions.rule: Every app lists an ask's versions under ⋯ → History, never as "Versions".

decisions.said: Images can sit between paragraphs of text, not only in table cells; no file path is ever shown for one.
decisions.rule: Every app draws an ask's picture between paragraphs as wide as the text, and never a file path for it.

decisions.said: The ask uses full width (full-width mode is always supported); no narrow column.
decisions.rule: Every app draws an ask at the full width it has, never in a narrow column.

decisions.said: Buttons size to their labels and overflow as units, wrapping only when a row is full, the native way on each platform.
decisions.rule: Every app sizes an ask's buttons to their labels and wraps them as whole buttons only when a row is full (Adw.WrapBox; Compose FlowRow).

decisions.said: Choices aren't tied to pictures explicitly; picture buttons are supported.
decisions.rule: Every app draws a button with a picture as a picture button; nothing else ties pictures to choices.

decisions.said: No expiry rules; form fields are supported in asks.
decisions.rule: No app expires an ask; every app draws an ask's form as setting rows.

decisions.said: Asks come from tasks only, for now.
decisions.rule: Every ask names its task and the task's Bot; no app raises one from a chat.

decisions.said: Pressing any button notifies the task, with the form's values; no separate Submit.
decisions.rule: Every app answers an ask by its buttons alone, sending the form's values with the one pressed.

decisions.said: When a model answers for the person, its answer is shown to confirm first, the ask staying until they do.
decisions.rule: Every app shows a model's answer for the person to confirm or change; it takes effect only as they press a button.

decisions.said: A typed message goes to the asking task's Bot, which can answer or post a new version.
decisions.rule: Every app sends what's written in an ask's box to the asking task's Bot.

decisions.said: Meta can help fill in the form of an ask you've selected, using its context.
decisions.rule: Every app's Meta can read the selected ask (body, form, buttons, task and run log, its Bot's chat) and fill its form for the person to check; it never presses a button.
